newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Top Asia-Pacific executives submit APEC proposals.
newsitem.headline: Top Asia-Pacific executives submit APEC proposals.

text.p: Top Asia-Pacific business leaders on Thursday presented a set of proposals they hope will be adopted at this year's APEC summit aimed at boosting trade and providing greater access to investment capital.
Members of the APEC Business Advisory Council presented their proposals to Philippine President Fidel Ramos, host of the November 25 summit.
Ramos has said one of his goals as summit chairman will be to give the private sector a higher profile in the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum.

If U.S. President Bill Clinton and the other heads of government meeting at Subic Bay north of Manila accept the ABAC proposals, they could be incorporated in an APEC action agenda to be announced at the end of the summit.
-- Create an APEC business visa and APEC business immigration lanes at airports to make business-related travel easier
-- Set up a central APEC registry for trademarks and standards to promote investment and technology flows.
-- Establish APEC Voluntary Investment Projects under which governments will provide enhanced investment protection.
-- Tackle the region's huge infrastructure by a series of round table conferences where government planners and the private sector can work to remove obstacles to investment.
-- Set up an APEC network for small and medium scale enterprises (SME) to help develop human resources, improve access to capital and credit and to market opportunities.
-- Support the holding of round table conferences in each economy bringing SME representatives together with government agencies, banks and other potential providers of apital and credit.
-- Set up statistical mechanisms for measuring the progress of SME development. --Manila newsroom (632) 841-8936
